sources.title: LGBTQ rights in Amazonas
sources.claim_summary: Lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and queer (LGBTQ) rights in the Brazilian state of Amazonas have had significant legal advances in recent decades. Homosexuality has been legal in the state, as well as throughout Brazil, since 1830.

records.name: Santa Catarina
records.summary_text: Direction: worse than national — the only Brazilian state in the country to have enacted a statutory bathroom restriction, and the venue of a nationally decisive refusal. A trans woman was refused entry to the women's bathroom by staff at a Florianópolis shopping centre, urinated on herself in front of shoppers and had to take public transport home; on 6 June 2024 the Supreme Federal Tribunal rejected her appeal, leaving these refusals lawful under ordinary private-premises rules — the legal exposure a visibly trans visitor faces using bathrooms in shops, restaurants and transport hubs.
